Definition: from G3956 and a derivative of G58; a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship:--general assembly.
BiblicalUsage: Panēgyris is the general assembly, the festive gathering of a whole people. The believer has come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this one verse lifts my eyes: my worship joins a festal gathering in heaven, the whole assembly of the firstborn, and I am already part of it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
